summary: Every value has a type, and the type decides what you can do with it. You can add numbers, but not names.
points: INTEGER holds whole numbers, and REAL holds decimals.
TEXT holds words. SQLite also stores dates as text, such as '2024-03-15'.
NULL means a value is missing. It isn't zero or empty text.
typeof(column) shows the type of each value.

example.sql:
SELECT name, salary, typeof(salary) AS salary_type, bonus, typeof(bonus) AS bonus_type
FROM employees;
example.explanation: salary is always an integer. bonus is an integer when present and null when missing.
